subject: botany_2
question_text: With reference to transportation of food within a plant, what are source and sink?

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.39, printed question 56. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

insider_note: Each half needs a definition AND an example. The examples are short, so there is no reason to leave them out.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Source
steps.margin_note: Definition plus one example. Three lines.
lines: The source is the place in the plant body
steps.why: Food is made where photosynthesis happens, so the leaf is the source by definition rather than by convention.
common_mistakes: Calling the root the source. The root usually stores food, so it is a sink.
Leaving out the example. The example is part of the mark.
steps.memory_tip: Source makes it, sink keeps it.

steps.label: Sink
steps.margin_note: Definition, examples, and one line on why the roles can swap.

lines.text: Source makes food; sink stores it

lines: The sink is the place in the plant body where
food material is STORED or used.
Source and sink can change with the season, so
phloem transport runs in both directions.
steps.why: A part can be a source in one season and a sink in another, which is why phloem transport is not fixed to one direction the way xylem transport is.
common_mistakes: Naming only one example. The question uses the plural.
Saying phloem always moves food downward. It moves toward whichever part is the sink.
steps.memory_tip: Whichever end is storing today is the sink today.
